title: Choose a safe work surface
body: • Do not use on an unstable surface or a tablecloth. • Take care where you set down the hot bread pan. (Risk of falling or fire.) • Do not use on carpets or other heat-sensitive coverings. (Risk of fire.) • Do not use on surfaces made slippery by flour, grease or dust. • Remove flour and other deposits and place at least 10 cm from the edge. (The appliance may slip and fall.) • Do not use close to walls or furniture. • Leave at least 5 cm clearance. (Risk of deformation or discolouration.)

• Do not touch hot parts such as the bread pan, appliance body, vents, interior, heater or inner lid. (Risk of burns.) → Always use oven mitts to remove the bread pan. • Do not use wet mitts. (They conduct heat readily and may cause burns.)
• Keep out of reach of young children. • Do not let children or people unfamiliar with the appliance use it unsupervised. (Risk of burns, electric shock or injury.)
• Measure ingredients and select programs correctly. (Dough that scatters or overflows can burn on the heater, producing smoke or causing a malfunction.)
• Do not immerse the appliance in water or splash it with water. (Risk of electric shock or fire from a short circuit.)
• Unplug when not in use. (Risk of electric shock or fire from electrical leakage.)
• Always hold the plug, not the cord, when unplugging. (Risk of electric shock or fire from a short circuit.)

• Do not cover the lid with a cloth or similar item. • Keep the handle lowered during use. • Do not place in a damp area or near a flame. • Do not apply excessive force to the parts shown on the right. (Risk of damage or deformation.)
• If you have food allergies, consult your doctor before use. • This appliance is not designed for use in vehicles, boats or outdoors.

title: Power supply and safety
body: Do not touch the steam vent.
• Take particular care around children. (Risk of burns.)
• Do not damage the power cord or plug.
Do not scratch, modify, place near hot surfaces, bend forcefully, twist, pull, place heavy objects on, bundle or pinch them.
If an abnormality or fault occurs, stop using the appliance immediately and unplug it. (Risk of smoke, fire, electric shock or injury.)

Examples of abnormalities or faults • The plug or cord becomes unusually hot. • The cord is damaged or power is intermittent. • The appliance becomes deformed or unusually hot. • An unusual rotating noise occurs during operation. → Ask your retailer to inspect and repair it immediately.

→ Consult your retailer for repairs. • Do not use a damaged cord or a loose outlet. (Risk of electric shock or fire from a short circuit.) • Do not connect or disconnect the plug with wet hands. (Risk of electric shock.)
• Use a dedicated 100 V AC outlet rated at 15 A or higher. (Risk of electric shock or fire.)
• Insert the plug fully. (Risk of smoke, fire or electric shock.)
• Remove dust from the plug regularly. (Dust on the pins can absorb moisture, compromise insulation and cause a fire.) → Unplug and wipe with a dry cloth.

title: Read the control panel
body: Menu ▲/▼ selects an automatic program. Dough selects a dough program.
Raisin sets additions. Crust selects crust colour. Timer sets the finish time.
Hour and Min set the clock, finish time or supported cooking time. Stage and Level are used for manual functions.
Start begins cooking or sets the timer. In manual operation it also pauses or resumes. Cancel resets settings. Press and hold Cancel to cancel after starting.
The supplied panel illustration is translated into English. Japanese legends require a Japanese panel reference.

title: Set the clock
body: Plug in the appliance. The clock uses a 24-hour format.
Press and hold Hour or Min. Release when you hear a beep and the time flashes.
Set the time while the display flashes. Hold the time button to advance quickly.
When the display stops flashing, the setting is complete. Unplug the appliance.

title: Weigh flour and water
body: • No need to sift. • Protein content varies, so different flours rise differently. • Always weigh flour. Do not use a measuring cup.
• Always weigh water. Do not use a measuring cup.

• Use cold water (about 5°C, like iced water) for: - Rapid white bread - Quick sweet bread - Rice French bread - French bread - Rye bread - Wholemeal bread - Brioche - Custom bread - Room temperatures of 25°C or above. • Alkaline water is unsuitable.
• When using milk, reduce the water by the same amount.

title: Load the pan for pain de mie
body: Remove the pan in the direction of the illustrated arrow. Push the kneading blade firmly onto the shaft. The shaft must be fully visible through the blade’s hole.

Mound the flour and other initial ingredients, except dry yeast, in the centre. Pour water around the edges. At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).
Put the pan back, turn it in the illustrated direction to lock it, and close the lid. The handle can stop partway down.
Blot any moisture from the yeast dispenser with a tissue. Rubbing may create static. Put moisture-free dry yeast in the dispenser.
Select program 1. Close both lids securely and press Start. For amounts and removal instructions, open the Pain de mie recipe.

title: Choose automatic or hand additions
body: You can add ingredients of your choice. Depending on the ingredients, select automatic dispensing (“Yes” on the display) or manual adding (“Yes ♪”).
• Put raisins, walnuts and similar ingredients in the raisin/nut dispenser for automatic dispensing.
• Ingredients that cannot be dispensed automatically, such as cheese and chocolate (p. 21), must be added by hand when the beeps sound.
• To retain the shape of added ingredients, select “Yes / Gentle mixing” or “Yes ♪ / Gentle mixing” (p. 22).
Follow each recipe’s ingredient quantities and limits for additions. Otherwise, ingredients may fly out of the pan and burn on the heater, causing odours or smoke.
Up to 100 g total in the dispenser.
• Spread ingredients level. Heaping them up may prevent the dispenser from opening.
• In summer or when using the timer, sugar-coated fruit may become sticky as the sugar melts, and may not dispense.

title: Timer & ingredients
body: Green peas, olives and ham / bacon carry the timer exclusion in the automatic dispenser table. They may spoil, especially in summer.
Sugar-coated fruit may become sticky and fail to dispense. Check the recipe and the manual’s tables before setting a delayed finish.

title: Set a delayed finish
body: Check the clock. Select a timer-compatible program.
If using Raisin or Crust colour, set them before the timer. Check the ingredients against the restrictions on printed page 20.
Press Timer. Use Hour and Min to choose the finish time within the program’s allowed range. Press and hold to advance quickly.
Press Start to set the timer. Example for pain de mie at 20:30: available finish times are 1:20–9:30 the next morning.

title: Knead levels and limits
body: Use individual stages of the bread-making process. Select Knead, Rise or Bake, then set the level and time. • When using Knead or Rise, check the dough’s condition as appropriate for the bread you are making.
Rotation speed levels for different tasks • Level 1: combining flour or making marbled dough • Level 2: low speed / mixing in extra ingredients • Level 3: medium speed • Level 4: high speed

• For 30 seconds after starting, or restarting after a pause, the blade turns slowly to prevent flour from scattering. It then changes to the selected speed. • The level can be changed after starting. During the first 30 seconds of slow rotation, however, the change takes effect only when that period has ended.
Time settings: Levels 1, 2 and 3: 1–30 minutes Level 4: 1–15 minutes

title: Rise levels and limits
body: Use individual stages of the bread-making process. Select Knead, Rise or Bake, then set the level and time. • When using Knead or Rise, check the dough’s condition as appropriate for the bread you are making.
Rising temperature levels for different uses • Level 1: resting / bench rest • Level 2: crusty breads • Level 3: white breads and enriched breads • Level 4: proofing after shaping / final proofing
• The level can be changed after starting.
Time settings: 10–120 minutes

title: Bake levels and limits
body: Use individual stages of the bread-making process. Select Knead, Rise or Bake, then set the level and time. • When using Knead or Rise, check the dough’s condition as appropriate for the bread you are making.

Baking temperature levels for different breads • Level 1: brioche / white breads (light crust) • Level 2: pain de mie / white breads (medium crust) • Level 3: rye / wholemeal / white breads (dark crust) • Level 4: French bread
• The level can be changed after starting.
Time settings: 30–50 minutes • If the bread is not baked enough when the program finishes, you can use Additional Baking. Additional baking: up to 2 times*
* Available until the total set baking time reaches 50 minutes. After 50 minutes, “U50” appears on the display and additional baking is unavailable. (p.101)

title: Run a manual knead
body: Press Stage to select Knead.
Press Level to select the rotation speed.
Set the kneading time.
• Set 1–30 minutes* in 1- minute increments.
* When Level 4 is selected: 1–15 minutes
Press Start.
• Press Start again to pause or resume.
• Pause / resume • Maximum pause: 15 minutes

• For 30 seconds after starting, or restarting after a pause, the blade turns slowly to prevent flour from scattering. It then changes to the selected speed. • The level can be changed after starting. During the first 30 seconds of slow rotation, however, the change takes effect only when that period has ended.

title: Run a manual rise
body: Press Stage to select Rise.
Press Level to select the rising temperature.
• Set 10–120 minutes in 5- minute increments.
Press Start.
• Press Start again to pause or resume.
• Pause / resume • Maximum pause: 15 minutes

title: Bake and extend baking
body: Press Stage to select Bake.
Press Level to select the baking temperature.
• Set 30–50 minutes* in 1- minute increments.
Press Start.
• Press Start again to pause or resume.
• Pause / resume • Maximum pause: 15 minutes
When the beeps sound, press Cancel and remove the bread pan. Let it cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread.

After baking, you can bake further until the total time, including the first bake, reaches 50 minutes. (For example, a 35-minute first bake allows 15 minutes of additional baking.) Repeat from step 1 on the left. • Additional baking can be selected for about 15 minutes after baking ends. It is unavailable once the oven chamber cools down.
■ You can also start Additional Baking as follows. • If you have not pressed Cancel in step 5 above: 1 Press the time button and set the baking time. 2 Press Start.
* For additional baking: 1–20 minutes

title: Save a My Knead pattern
body: Press Dough to choose P1, P2, P3, P4 or P5.

Press Stage to select Sequence A. Press Level to choose the rotation speed, then set the kneading time in 1-minute increments. Levels 1–3 allow 1–30 minutes. Across all stages, Level 4 must total 15 minutes or less.
For another stage, press Stage to select b and set its level and time. Repeat for C if needed.
Press Start to save the pattern and begin.

title: Recall or change My Knead
body: Press Dough to display the saved My Knead number.
Use Stage to check Sequences b and C.
Press Start to begin. During operation press Stage to view the current sequence and its remaining time.
To overwrite a pattern, repeat the save procedure. To restore the previous settings before starting, press Cancel.

title: Wash and dry parts

Alkaline or mildly alkaline cleaners
Nylon side of a sponge / mesh-covered sponge
Scouring powder Metal scourer

title: Bread pan and blades
body: Remove any remaining dough and rinse with water.
1 Pour warm water into the bread pan and leave it to soak for a while.
• If the blade is difficult to remove, turn it left and right, then pull it off.
2 Thoroughly wash the bread pan and blade with water and a sponge.
• If there is a white film on the blade, wash it with mild dishwashing detergent. Residue makes dough more likely to stick and can leave the blade inside the loaf.
• Do not leave dough around the mounting shaft. This can damage the pan’s fluororesin coating.
3 Use a bamboo skewer to remove dough caught in the blade or mounting shaft.
• Dough left on the mounting shaft can make the blade come off more easily or remain inside the loaf.

title: Lid and dispensing valve
body: Wipe with a well- wrung damp cloth.
• After wiping the dispensing valve with a damp cloth, check that the ingredient opening is closed.

title: Starter container
body: Wash thoroughly with mild dishwashing detergent and dry.
• Starter residue allows bacteria to multiply and cause spoilage, preventing the next starter batch from developing properly.
■ If spoilage occurs: 1 Soak in diluted chlorine-based kitchen bleach. 2 Rinse thoroughly.

title: Upper lid
body: Remove and wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth.
• Open to 70–90° and pull upwards.

title: Yeast dispenser
body: Wipe with a well-wrung damp cloth and allow to air-dry.
Do not dry-wipe the yeast dispenser!
Static electricity may prevent the yeast from dropping.

title: Raisin/nut dispenser
body: Remove and wash with mild dishwashing detergent.
• Pull upwards.
• Press to open the flap. • Remove all oily residue.

title: Main unit and steam vent
body: Wipe with a well- wrung damp cloth.
• Remove flour, ingredients and extra ingredients scattered inside the oven chamber. • Oil residue or water droplets may collect around the steam vent.

title: U50 · Hot chamber or additional baking limit
body: The oven chamber is hot (40°C or above), for example after baking. Open the lid and allow the oven chamber to cool thoroughly (about 1 hour immediately after completion).
In manual Bake mode, this message also appears when additional baking has been used twice or the total time has exceeded 50 minutes.

title: U53 · Motor overloaded
body: The motor is overloaded.
Measure the ingredients accurately. Crush large pieces, such as walnuts, before adding them. (Press Cancel.)

title: Yeast does not drop

Use fresh dry yeast or dried natural yeast.

• Are the ingredients heaped up? Spread them level.

If it stopped while still at the dough stage, the dough can be reused. (p.91)

title: Frequently asked questions continued

Can I bake a square- topped loaf? This bread maker produces domed loaves: the dough expands upwards during baking (oven spring). How can I slice bread neatly? Bread is difficult to slice straight after baking. Wait a little before slicing. • Lay the loaf on its side and move a bread knife back and forth. If it is still difficult to remove after taking out the bread pan and letting it cool for about 2 minutes, return the pan to the machine for 5–10 minutes, then try again. White bread Slice, wrap each slice individually in plastic wrap and freeze. For the best flavour, freeze bread while it is as fresh as possible. Can I freeze bread or dough? After baking / completion • For best flavour, keep frozen for about one month. Butter rolls After shaping and proofing, arrange on a tray, cover with plastic wrap and freeze. Once frozen, transfer to a plastic bag. To bake, thaw at 30–35°C, brush with beaten egg and bake. • If short of time, brush with beaten egg while still frozen and add about 5 minutes to the baking time.
